outcomes: A workload with several datasources is modeled by construction, with no single-DSN convention
No secret can reach the infra requirements, because a requirement has no member that could carry one
Go and TypeScript code reach a datasource by its logical name, whatever transport the deployer chose
nonGoals: Opening a connection or importing a driver: the framework database adapters build the driver from a binding
Applying migrations at startup: the migration protocol owns that
Docker auto-provisioning for mode auto, which no provider implements yet

requirements.text: A requirement manifest names each datasource's engine and schema and has no connection member, so strict parsing refuses one and no host, user, password or DSN can reach a requirement. Every requirement fixture gets its verdict.

A binding gives each logical datasource its engine, its schema and a connection, and a datasource without a connection is refused. Every binding fixture gets its verdict, and a valid binding survives a marshal and a re-parse unchanged.

A connection selects exactly one transport: a self-contained dsn; a TCP host with its port, database, user, password, ssl and params; or a cloud socket instance with its database, user, password and params. No transport, two transports, or a member of another transport is refused.

A test binding is a binding plus a policy: mode skip, require or auto; isolation database or schema; reuse none or bundle-template; and the applyMigrations and keepDatabases flags. The engine is postgres. A value outside a set is refused, and every test binding fixture gets its verdict.

The three shapes parse strictly. Malformed JSON, an unknown member, a protocolVersion other than 1, an invalid datasource name or schema, a missing engine, schema or connection, and a nil document are refused, each with an error code under database.
Project flattens a requirement manifest into a name, an engine and schemas per datasource, sorted by datasource name, and adds no implicit schema.
The requirement, binding and test binding schemas carry exactly the members of the Go types, connection included, require what the Go validators require, and pin protocolVersion to the Go constant.

The Go database adapter reads bindings through this module. It builds a named datasource's pool from its one transport, refuses a binding the protocol refuses, resolves the DATABASE_BINDINGS document and falls through when it is unset, and derives its infra entry through the projection.

The Go test provider reads a test binding through this module: an absent binding follows the mode, which defaults to require. It isolates each datasource by database or by schema, and it passes the datasource selection corpus in conformance/test-provider-datasources.json, provisioning only the datasources a suite names.

The TypeScript adapter of @putnami/database parses a binding strictly: it accepts a valid binding with several datasources and refuses another protocolVersion, a connection with two transports, a dsn with ssl, an engine other than postgres, a missing schema and a non-canonical datasource name. It reads the binding from DATABASE_BINDINGS, and resolves nothing when the document is absent or blank.

The TypeScript test provider of @putnami/database follows the mode when no datasource is bound: skip skips and require fails naming DATABASE_TEST_BINDINGS. It passes the datasource selection corpus in conformance/test-provider-datasources.json: it plans only the datasources a suite names, and a name the binding lacks skips or fails as each case expects.
